Context/Background:
Circular RNA (circRNA) is a class of noncoding RNA with regulatory potentials. Here, we identified circRMST as an exceptionally abundant circRNA predominantly expressed in neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC) and small cell lung cancer (SCLC), with strong conservation between humans and mice.

To explore the functional role of circRMST, we designed two shRNAs targeting the backspliced junction (BSJ), achieving 70%–93% knockdown efficiency. In 3D Matrigel-embedded cultures, circRMST knockdown significantly impaired cell growth across three NEPC and four SCLC-A models. Additionally, cell cycle analysis in SHP77 cells revealed cell-cycle arrest. In vivo, SHP77 xenografts in NSG immunodeficient mice exhibited markedly reduced tumor growth upon circRMST depletion.
Prompt:
To investigate transcriptional changes following circRMST knockdown, we performed RNA-seq in SHP77 cells and identified hundreds of differentially expressed genes.

What are the most relevant pathways in a GSEA results with the differential gene list?  Nominate a target most relevant for neuroendocrine prostate cancer.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
To probe the role of circRMST in NEPC, Teng et al. performed RNA-seq in SHP77 cells following circRMST knockdown (two shRNAs; 70%–93% KD). Differential expression (DE) analysis (shRNA1 vs control and shRNA2 vs control) yielded ~9 000 and ~8 000 significant genes (|log2FC| up to ~3.4; padj = 0.0). Key DE down-regulated NEPC markers included ASCL1, GRP, CD24, NTSR1; up-regulated stress and adhesion regulators included SESN3, FTH1, ITGB1. No raw counts or replicate numbers specified. GSEA (preranked by mean log2FC) was run on the aggregated DE list to identify enriched pathways across four libraries.

Keywords  
• Neuroendocrine differentiation  
• GPCR signaling  
• Cell-cycle/mitosis  
• Unfolded protein response  

Candidate Genes  
ASCL1, NTSR1, GRP, SSTR3, AURKA, SESN3, FTH1, ITGB1

Pathway Enrichments  
Counts by database:  
• KEGG_2016: 10 up, 11 down (47.6% up, 52.4% down; ratio 0.91)  
• GO_Biological_Process_2023: 171 up, 118 down (59.2% up, 40.8% down; ratio 1.45)  
• Reactome_Pathways_2024: 104 up, 53 down (66.2% up, 33.8% down; ratio 1.96)  
• MSigDB_Hallmark_2020: 7 up, 1 down (87.5% up, 12.5% down; ratio 7.0)

KEGG_2016 (UP)  
| Theme                            | Direction | Leading Genes                             |  
|----------------------------------|-----------|-------------------------------------------|  
| Protein processing in ER (hsa04141)        | Up        | CUL1;CAPN2;DNAJB11;CRYAB;SEL1L;…   |  
| Lysosome (hsa04142)                     | Up        | GAA;CTSF;ACP2;GALNS;CTSA;…             |  

KEGG_2016 (DOWN)  
| Theme                             | Direction | Leading Genes                             |  
|-----------------------------------|-----------|-------------------------------------------|  
| Neuroactive ligand-receptor interaction (hsa04080) | Down      | ADRA2A;ADRA1A;PRLHR;GABBR2;SSTR3;… |  
| Calcium signaling pathway (hsa04020)           | Down      | CACNA1B;ADRA1A;SPHK1;ERBB3;…           |  

GO_Biological_Process_2023 (UP)  
| Theme                            | Direction | Leading Genes           |  
|----------------------------------|-----------|-------------------------|  
| Regulation Of Fibroblast Migration (GO:0010762) | Up        | DDR2;ITGB1;PRKCE      |  
| Glycogen Metabolic Process (GO:0005977)          | Up        | GAA;PRKAG2;PER2       |  

GO_Biological_Process_2023 (DOWN)  
| Theme                       | Direction | Leading Genes                     |  
|-----------------------------|-----------|-----------------------------------|  
| Neuropeptide Signaling Pathway (GO:0007218) | Down      | GAL;SSTR2;GRP;NTS;…           |  
| Morphogenesis Of An Epithelium (GO:0002009)  | Down      | SOX9;AIRE;FGFR2;SOX8;LHX1    |  

Reactome_Pathways_2024 (UP)  
| Theme                    | Direction | Leading Genes                   |  
|--------------------------|-----------|---------------------------------|  
| EGFR Downregulation      | Up        | SH3GL1;EGF;HBEGF;EGFR;…     |  

Reactome_Pathways_2024 (DOWN)  
| Theme                    | Direction | Leading Genes                           |  
|--------------------------|-----------|------------------------------------------|  
| GPCR Ligand Binding      | Down      | ADRA2A;ADRA1A;PRLHR;HCRTR1;…       |  
| GPCR Downstream Signalling | Down    | RGS4;ADRA1A;ADRA2A;GABBR2;…       |  

MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (UP)  
| Theme               | Direction | Leading Genes                                |  
|---------------------|-----------|----------------------------------------------|  
| mTORC1 Signaling    | Up        | TCEA1;CCT6A;GPI;YKT6;EIF2S2;…        |  
| Mitotic Spindle     | Up        | ROCK1;CEP131;SOS1;KIF1B;…            |  
| Unfolded Protein Response | Up  | EIF2S1;EXOC2;KIF5B;DNAJC3;…       |  
| G2-M Checkpoint     | Up        | NUP50;CUL1;UCK2;TFDP1;…         |  

MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (DOWN)  
| Theme              | Direction | Leading Genes               |  
|--------------------|-----------|-----------------------------|  
| KRAS Signaling Dn  | Down      | RGS11;CHST2;MYO15A;…    |  

Analysis  
Across libraries, GPCR-related pathways dominate down-regulated terms (KEGG neuroactive ligand–receptor interaction, Reactome GPCR binding/signalling; strong negative NES). In contrast, ER stress, lysosomal function, cell-cycle (G2-M, mitotic spindle) and mTORC1 signalling are up-regulated. This pattern reflects decreased neuroendocrine-peptide/GPCR signaling alongside activation of proteostasis and proliferative control pathways upon circRMST KD. The polarization of GPCR suppression (Reactome down ratio 66%) vs. cell-cycle/UPR induction (Hallmark up ratio 87.5%) suggests a switch from NEPC signaling toward a growth-arrest/stress phenotype.

Targeted Subset (GPCR terms)  
Filtered GSEA for “GPCR” yields:  
| Data Base                  | Pathway                 | NES    | Leading Genes (→ NTSR1,…,GRP,ASCL1 ) |  
|----------------------------|-------------------------|--------|-----------------------------------------|  
| Reactome_Pathways_2024     | GPCR Ligand Binding     | -4.141 | ADRA2A;ADRA1A;PRLHR;HCRTR1;…;NTSR1;GRP… |  
| Reactome_Pathways_2024     | GPCR Downstream Signalling | -3.268 | RGS4;ADRA1A;ADRA2A;GABBR2;…;NTSR1;GRP… |  

Both show very high negative NES and include NTSR1 and GRP—key neuropeptide receptors in NEPC.

Key Genes/Proteins (leading-edge)  
Up-regulated leading-edge  
| Gene   | Direction | Role/Function                          | Pathway(s)                          |  
|--------|-----------|----------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|  
| FTH1   | Up        | Ferritin heavy chain (iron storage)    | “Golgi Associated Vesicle Biogenesis” (Reactome low set) |  
| SESN3  | Up        | Stress-induced sestrin; ROS regulation | mTORC1 Signaling (Hallmark)         |  
| ITGB1  | Up        | β1-integrin (adhesion)                 | Regulation Of Fibroblast Migration (GO_BP) |  

Down-regulated leading-edge  
| Gene   | Direction | Role/Function                                     | Pathway(s)                            |  
|--------|-----------|---------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|  
| NTSR1  | Down      | Neurotensin GPCR                                  | GPCR Ligand Binding (Reactome); Neuropeptide Signaling (GO_BP) |  
| GRP    | Down      | Gastrin-releasing peptide (bombesin-like)         | Neuropeptide Signaling (GO_BP)        |  
| ASCL1  | Down      | BHLH transcription factor (NEPC lineage driver)   | Neuron Differentiation (GO_BP)        |  

Among these, NTSR1 stands out—strongly down (log2FC_sh1 = -5.01; sh2 = -4.10), central in GPCR ligand binding, and highly cited in NEPC contexts (PMID 30770901; 25581609).

Implications & Next Steps  
1. Validate NTSR1 as a therapeutic node in NEPC: test NTSR1 antagonists or knockdown in vivo.  
2. Investigate whether UPR/mTORC1 activation upon circRMST KD creates vulnerabilities—e.g., combine with proteasome or mTOR inhibitors.  
3. Clarify circRMST’s mechanism: does it scaffold NEPC-specific GPCR mRNA or compete for miRNAs?  
4. Examine ASCL1 modulation post-KD to confirm NEPC lineage reprogramming.  

References  
1. PMID 30770901  
2. PMID 25581609
